details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:389-404 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The runtime copy still uses word-level deferral matching, so unrelated deferral words or “retry until” phrasing can make an unanswered retry instruction appear to be a limit wait.
  WHY: The pickup executes this root script, and the false classification can cause it to resume a session that should be skipped as needs_input.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:240-249 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The retry forms accept a bare time as the deferral target, so a retry instruction not tied to the limit reset can be classified as a limit wait.
  WHY: This violates the reset-tied, fail-closed contract; the highest severity is critical, though reviewers disagreed, rating it from NIT to BLOCKER.
- tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py:29-31, 997-998 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Selector tests import the template twin rather than exercising the runtime copy that the pickup invokes.
  WHY: The parity test detects that the files differ, but behavioral tests do not verify the runtime copy.
- tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py:268-380 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The tests omit cases combining limit text with retry instructions deferred to a bare time.
  WHY: The existing “Retry after 5pm” case lacks limit keywords, so the suite does not test whether the classifier rejects a bare-time retry after the other gates pass.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:206, 396-399 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The runtime deferral pattern omits “after” and singular “reset,” causing “Retry after the reset” not to be recognized as a limit wait.
  WHY: The pickup treats this legitimate deferred retry as needs_input, leaving the session stopped until a human resumes it.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:482-496 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: A “then” sentence is accepted only after a wait or reset sentence, so a consecutive “Then retry again” sentence makes an otherwise valid sequence fail closed.
  WHY: A genuinely deferred retry sequence can be skipped and require manual intervention.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:247, 479-480 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The “then” form does not accept an “and” prefix, so “And then retry” as a separate sentence is not recognized.
  WHY: The classifier fails closed and skips a genuinely waiting session, requiring manual operator intervention.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: “The root `.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py` follows its `workflow-templates/.claude/` twin through the twin sync.”
  expected_change_site: .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The root script retains word-level deferral logic and patterns while the twin uses sentence-level closed forms; the runtime pickup executes the root script; test_template_parity fails until the copies match.
- requirement: “tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py pins each rule above,” including that a retry not tied to the reset fails closed.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py, test_is_limit_wait and test_a_limit_wait_that_also_asks_a_human_is_skipped parametrize tables
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: Neither table includes a case combining limit text with a retry deferred to a bare time; “Retry after 5pm” does not pass the names-limit check.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  WHY: The pickup executes the root copy; this can cause a resume trigger for a session that should be skipped as needs_input.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: _limit_wait_forms retry_forms at lines 240-243 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A retry at a bare time can match without tying that time to a limit reset.
  WHY: This is a contract mismatch; the reviewer assessed the practical risk as near zero.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: is_limit_wait lines 396-399, LIMIT_DEFERRAL_PATTERN at line 206 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The deferral pattern omits “after” and singular “reset,” so “Retry after the reset” is not classified as a limit wait.
  WHY: The session is skipped as needs_input and stays stopped until manually resumed.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: _limit_wait_sentence_kind at lines 482-496 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A “then” sentence after another “then” sentence is rejected, so a sequence ending in “Then retry again” fails closed.
  WHY: A genuinely deferred sequence can be skipped and require manual intervention.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The root .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py follows its workflow-templates/.claude/ twin through the twin sync" (PR description, changelog.d/6102-skip-unanswered-question-resumes.md:16)
  Expected change site: .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py
  Evidence of absence: The root copy's is_limit_wait at lines 389-404 uses word-level deferral matching (LIMIT_DEFERRAL_PATTERN.search anywhere in text, LIMIT_WAIT_START_PATTERN + LIMIT_WORD_PATTERN + LIMIT_WAIT_WORD_PATTERN fallback). The twin's is_limit_wait at lines 447-469 uses sentense-level closed-form matching via _limit_wait_forms, _limit_wait_sentense, and _limit_wait_sentense_kind. The root copy still defines LIMIT_WAIT_WORD_PATTERN, LIMIT_WAIT_START_PATTERN, LIMIT_RETRY_WORD_PATTERN, and LIMIT_DEFERRAL_PATTERN at lines 163-206 which the twin dropped in review round 3. The PR description states "The root .claude/ copy follows through the twin sync" and the progress log says "held for the fourth twin sync," confirming the gap is known but not yet resolved in this PR.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
